title: Node.js APIs and TypeScript knowledge check

questions.prompt: What belongs in a production backend type boundary?
options: Log credentials so failed requests can be reproduced.
Validate requests, authorize the action on the server, handle failures and preserve data-integrity invariants.
Trust a client TypeScript interface as an access-control mechanism.
questions.answer_key: Validate requests, authorize the action on the server, handle failures and preserve data-integrity invariants.
questions.explanation: Backend runtime behavior and authorization must be enforced on the server, independent of client types.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Node.js APIs and TypeScript”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with file operations and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with file operations and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “File operations”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Node.js APIs and TypeScript”?
options: Assume typing operating-system interactions is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check streams and buffers, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check streams and buffers, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Streams and buffers”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
